pages.title: Prescriptions
pages.content:
Prescriptions

How a prescription
is talked through.

New prescriptions are usually ready in 20 minutes. Repeat prescriptions are ready within 24 hours.

Five steps

From hand-in to a call two weeks later

Every prescription at Megumi Pharmacy is checked against your record and then talked through by name, whether it arrived on paper, from your doctor, or as a repeat.

Hand it in

Bring a paper prescription to the counter, ask your doctor to send an e-prescription, or request a repeat by phone or by email at counter@megumipharmacy.example. Grace Liu takes it in at the front counter and confirms the name on the record before it goes any further. You do not need to decide on the spot whether you want a weekly blister pack or delivery.

Say if you would like either, and we will tell you the fee before we proceed: blister packs are $6.00 per week, and home delivery is $4.00 within 3 km. Pickup at the counter has no delivery charge.

We check it against your record

Before anything is prepared, a pharmacist checks the prescription against your record. We look at allergies and at the other medicines you already take, including ones from another prescriber if they are on the file. The check takes about ten minutes. If something does not match, we pause and ask you, or we call the prescriber.

We would rather hold the prescription than fill a line we cannot explain. Bring the boxes you still have at home if you are unsure what is current. That is the same habit we use in a medicine review.

Prepared and double-checked

Samuel Brandt, pharmacy technician, prepares the prescription in the dispensary. He checks the printed label against the plain box before it is bagged. A pharmacist then checks the same item again. Two pairs of eyes is the ordinary standard here, not an extra you have to request.

If the medicine is new to you, the bag waits at the counter until someone has time to talk it through. Dispensing is $9.95 per item. All prices are in Canadian dollars. We do not sell prescription medicines through the online shop.

Talked through at the counter

When the prescription is ready, we talk it through at the counter, or in the consultation room if you would rather sit down. Daniel Osei often takes new medicines and inhalers. He will show you how to hold a device, and he will ask you to show it back.

Leila Haddad takes longer lists into the consultation room. We use the name of the medicine and the time of day, and we write the point down if the label alone is not enough. Questions are welcome at this step. The queue can wait a few minutes.

A call two weeks later

For every new long-term medicine, we telephone two weeks later. The call is short. We ask whether the directions still make sense and whether anything on the label has been hard to follow. We do not ask you to report a result we can promise, because we do not promise one.

If the medicine is not new and not long-term, we will not invent a follow-up. If you miss the call, phone (416) 555-0148 and ask for the pharmacist who dispensed it. The same six people are here through the week, so the name on the bag is a person you can ask for.

Sending it

Ways to send a prescription

Paper is the simplest. Hand it to Grace at the counter during opening hours and we will start the record check while you wait or while you shop nearby. An e-prescription comes straight from your doctor. Tell the prescriber Megumi Pharmacy, 1184 Queen Street East, Toronto, and leave a phone number where we can reach you if a line needs a question.

A repeat can be requested by phone at (416) 555-0148 or by email at counter@megumipharmacy.example. Say the medicine name and how many days you have left. We will tell you if the repeat is still valid.

Plan your visit

Timing

When it is ready

A new prescription is usually ready in 20 minutes. A repeat prescription is ready within 24 hours. Both times are the usual pace. If the record check raises a question for your doctor, we will say so before you leave and we will call when it is actually ready. Monday to Friday we are open 8:30–19:00, Saturday 9:00–17:00, and Sunday 10:00–14:00.

Statutory holidays are closed, so a repeat requested before a holiday may be ready the next open day, still inside the ordinary 24 hours of opening. Ask at the counter if you need it sooner.

pages.content:
Services & fees

Every service,
with its price.

Prices are in Canadian dollars and are the same on every visit.

Every day

Three things we do every day

Prescriptions are dispensed at $9.95 per item, then talked through at the counter. Weekly blister packs, for people who want each day set out, are prepared by Samuel Brandt at $6.00 per week. Medicine reviews are Leila Haddad’s work: 30 minutes, by appointment, $35.00. Bring every box you take.

Vaccinations and travel health are Ana Kovač’s work, in the consultation room. A flu vaccination is $25.00. A travel health consultation is $45.00 for 30 minutes, and travel vaccines are charged at cost in addition to the consultation. None of these are sold as promises about results.

Booking

What to ask for

Ask for a prescription to be filled, a blister pack, a medicine review, a blood pressure check, a flu vaccination, a travel consultation, or delivery. The blood pressure check is the only free service, and you can ask for it at the counter without booking. Reviews and travel consultations need an appointment because each one is 30 minutes in the consultation room.

Flu vaccinations are given in that same room. Book at the counter or by phone at (416) 555-0148. If you are not sure which service you need, say what you came in with and we will name the one that fits.

pages.title: Medicine reviews
pages.content:
Medicine reviews

One list for
every medicine you take.

Thirty minutes in the consultation room with Leila Haddad. $35.00, by appointment.

A review

What happens in thirty minutes

Bring every medicine you take. In 30 minutes, by appointment, Leila Haddad turns the boxes into one written list and gives you a copy.

Bring everything

A medicine review is 30 minutes with Leila Haddad, by appointment, for $35.00. Bring every medicine you take: boxes, bottles, inhalers, and anything you buy for yourself. A shopping bag is a perfectly ordinary way to carry them. Leila meets you at the round table in the consultation room, with your list between you.

The fee is $35.00 for the half hour. All prices are in Canadian dollars. If you take medicines from more than one prescriber, bring those too. We can only talk through what is actually on the table.

One list

Leila checks each item against your record and writes one list: the name, the time of day, and whether it is still current. Duplicate boxes are marked, not thrown away, until a prescriber has confirmed a change. The point of the visit is one list instead of a cupboard of boxes you no longer trust.

Ruth, who is 78, came with twelve boxes in a shopping bag and left with that kind of list. Her story is “One list instead of twelve boxes.” She said she felt more confident laying her medicines out. We do not claim any other outcome.

What changes, your copy, and a follow-up call

Leila does not start or stop a prescribed medicine on her own in the room. If something should change, she writes the question for your doctor and tells you what she is asking. You leave with your own copy of the list, and the pharmacy keeps a copy with your record. After the review she telephones, as she does two weeks after every new long-term medicine, to ask whether the list is clear.

Call (416) 555-0148 to book. The room has been here since 2011. Hours are Monday to Friday 8:30–19:00, Saturday 9:00–17:00, and Sunday 10:00–14:00.

pages.title: Vaccinations & travel
pages.content:
Vaccinations & travel

Vaccinations,
talked through first.

Flu vaccination $25.00. Travel health consultation $45.00, vaccines at cost.

Flu

Flu

Ana Kovač gives flu vaccinations in the consultation room. The fee is $25.00. She will tell you what the vaccination is, and you can ask questions before she begins. The room is quiet, with a chair and a few minutes to sit afterward. Book at the counter or by phone at (416) 555-0148.

Clinics run from 1 October, as posted in the notice dated 2026.10.01. You do not need a long appointment for a flu vaccination, but booking keeps the room free. All prices are in Canadian dollars. We do not promise how you will feel afterward.

Travel

Travel consultation

A travel health consultation with Ana is $45.00 and lasts 30 minutes. Bring the dates of the trip and any vaccines you have already had, if you know them. She talks through what the trip needs and what this pharmacy can give. It is a planning conversation two weeks before a flight, or earlier if you have the dates.

A couple booked exactly that conversation before they flew. The story is “Two weeks before the flight.” They left knowing what to carry and when to come back for what Ana could prepare. No result beyond that conversation is promised.

Aftercare

Travel vaccines, records, and aftercare

Travel vaccines are charged at cost in addition to the $45.00 consultation. Ana records what was given and gives you a copy for your own papers. Aftercare is explained before you leave: what is ordinary, and what should bring you back to the counter or to a doctor.

If you need a record of a flu vaccination later, ask at the counter and we will read it from the file. Book at the counter or by phone. The pharmacy is open Monday to Friday 8:30–19:00, Saturday 9:00–17:00, and Sunday 10:00–14:00, and closed on statutory holidays.

pages.title: People
pages.content:
People

Six people,
one counter.

The same faces are at the counter each week.

People

Six people, one counter.

Megumi Ward & Daniel Osei

Founder & pharmacist · Pharmacist manager

Megumi Ward is founder and pharmacist. She opened the pharmacy in 2006 and still stands at the counter she planned, stone coat, short grey hair, in front of the light oak drawers. She knows the regulars by name and will slow a handover if a label is new. Daniel Osei is pharmacist manager. Inhalers and new medicines are his daily work. He shows a teenager how to hold an inhaler with a spacer, then asks to see it done again. If a device is hard to use, he would rather spend the extra minutes at the counter end than send you home uncertain.

Leila Haddad & Ana Kovač

Medicine reviews · Vaccinations & travel

Leila Haddad is the pharmacist who leads medicine reviews. She sits at the small round table in the consultation room with the boxes and a written list between her and you. A review is $35.00, 30 minutes, by appointment. She writes one list and gives you a copy. Ana Kovač is the pharmacist for vaccinations and travel health. She gives the flu vaccination for $25.00 and the travel consultation for $45.00, 30 minutes, with vaccines at cost. Both of them book the consultation room so the counter can keep moving while a longer talk happens next door.

Samuel Brandt & Grace Liu

Pharmacy technician · Pharmacy assistant

Samuel Brandt is pharmacy technician. He prepares prescriptions and the weekly blister packs, then a pharmacist checks his work. You will see him in the dispensary matching a printed label to a plain box. Blister packs are $6.00 per week. Grace Liu is pharmacy assistant at the front counter, in her twenties, and she also takes deliveries out. She hands you the paper bag, takes a repeat request, and will tell you if a pharmacist needs to speak before you go. Home delivery with Grace’s run is $4.00 within 3 km. She is the person who answers (416) 555-0148 first.

A Tuesday

A Tuesday, 8:30 to 19:00

On a Tuesday the door opens at 8:30. Grace is already at the front counter, and the first repeat requests are in the book. Samuel is in the dispensary with the morning baskets. Megumi walks the counter once before the street fills, checking who is due a two-week call. Daniel takes the inhaler lessons toward the middle of the day, when a teenager can come after school. Leila’s review appointments sit in the consultation room, half an hour each.

Ana keeps the flu clinic and any travel visit inside the same room when the calendar says so. At 19:00 the door closes on the weekday. Saturday is 9:00–17:00 and Sunday is 10:00–14:00. The six names on the Tuesday rota are the six names all week. That is the point of a small pharmacy. You should not have to retell the whole story to a stranger every time the bag is light.

Questions

Ask at the counter.

Phone (416) 555-0148 or email counter@megumipharmacy.example. A pharmacist is at the counter Mon–Fri 8:30–19:00, Sat 9:00–17:00 and Sun 10:00–14:00. All prices in Canadian dollars.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

An independent pharmacy
since 2006.

1184 Queen Street East, Toronto, near the streetcar stop.

Story

An independent counter since 2006

Megumi Ward opened Megumi Pharmacy in 2006 at 1184 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1L4. She wanted an independent community pharmacy where a person could hear their own name and have a new medicine talked through before they left. The shop is still a small counter on the neighbourhood high street, with the same purpose.

Six people work here, and the faces at the counter are the ones you meet week after week. You can reach the counter at (416) 555-0148 or counter@megumipharmacy.example.

Meet the people

At the counter

How we work at the counter

A paper prescription, an e-prescription from your doctor, or a repeat request by phone or email all start the same way. We check the medicine against your record, including allergies and anything else you take. That check takes about ten minutes. Samuel Brandt prepares the item and a pharmacist checks it again.

We then talk it through at the counter or in the consultation room. For every new long-term medicine, we call two weeks later. A new prescription is usually ready in 20 minutes. A repeat is ready within 24 hours. We say usually, because a question about the record can take longer.

Twenty years

Twenty years, five marks

The pharmacy opened in 2006. In 2011 we added the consultation room, so a longer conversation could happen away from the queue. In 2015 Samuel began the weekly blister-pack service, prepared each week. In 2019 we started home delivery, now $4.00 within 3 km.

In 2024 the team became the six of us: Megumi Ward, Daniel Osei, Leila Haddad, Ana Kovač, Samuel Brandt and Grace Liu. Hours have stayed steady: Monday to Friday 8:30–19:00, Saturday 9:00–17:00, Sunday 10:00–14:00. Statutory holidays are closed.

Our promise

What we will not do

We do not pressure you to buy something you did not come in for. The counter shelf is short, and a pharmacist can tell you to leave an item there. We do not promise results. A medicine review, a vaccination or a talk about a new inhaler is a careful conversation about the medicine in front of you.

The information on this site is general and does not replace advice from your pharmacist or doctor. If something on a label is unclear, bring it back and we will go through it by name.

Questions

Ask at the counter.

Phone (416) 555-0148 or email counter@megumipharmacy.example. A pharmacist is at the counter Mon–Fri 8:30–19:00, Sat 9:00–17:00 and Sun 10:00–14:00. All prices in Canadian dollars.

Plan your visit

Address

Address, phone, and hours

Megumi Pharmacy is at 1184 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1L4, Canada, near the streetcar stop. Phone (416) 555-0148. Email counter@megumipharmacy.example. Monday to Friday 8:30–19:00. Saturday 9:00–17:00. Sunday 10:00–14:00. Statutory holidays are closed. The shopfront is a high-street front with large windows.

Come to the counter for prescriptions, reviews, vaccinations, a free blood pressure check, or the short shelf of helpers. If you need a 30-minute visit, book the consultation room before you travel, so Leila or Ana has the chair held.

Getting here

By streetcar, on foot, or by bike

The pharmacy sits on Queen Street East near the streetcar stop, so the streetcar is the simplest way from along the street. The shopfront is easy to pick out in the morning: large clear windows, a bench, and often a bicycle outside. On foot, you are already on the high street. The door opens onto the bright floor, with low shelves and the pale stone counter ahead.

By bike, there is space to leave a bicycle at the front. We do not publish a route number or a distance beyond what you can see from the stop. If you are unsure you have the right door, the address is 1184.

Access

By car, and the step-free entrance

By car, use the high street and come in through the same front door as everyone else. We do not list a private lot or a parking fee, because we do not run one. The entrance is step-free. Inside, the counter is the low pale stone one you can see from the door, and the consultation room is the door ajar at the back of the floor.

If you use a wheelchair or a walker, say so when you call and Grace will watch for you at 8:30 or whenever you are due. Statutory holidays the door stays shut even if the street is busy.

Delivery

Home delivery

Home delivery is $4.00 within 3 km. Grace Liu takes deliveries from the front counter. It suits a repeat that is ready within 24 hours when the walk is difficult. Prescription pickup at the counter has no delivery fee. Shop items can be picked up free or delivered for the same $4.00 within 3 km.

We do not deliver prescription medicines bought online, because we do not sell prescription medicines online. Call (416) 555-0148 or email counter@megumipharmacy.example and give the address. If it is outside 3 km, we will say so and keep the bag at the counter for you.

The counter shelf

Ask at the counter.

Phone (416) 555-0148 or email counter@megumipharmacy.example. A pharmacist is at the counter Mon–Fri 8:30–19:00, Sat 9:00–17:00 and Sun 10:00–14:00. All prices in Canadian dollars.

pages.title: Shop
pages.content:
Shop

Small things
by the till.

Chosen by the pharmacists. No medicines are sold online; pickup at the counter is free.

The shelf

A short shelf, chosen by the pharmacists

We keep a short shelf of things that help around medicines. The pharmacists choose them, and they are sold without fuss. Nothing on this shelf is a prescription medicine. If you are not sure an item fits what you were told to use, ask at the counter before you pay.

Pickup at the counter is free. Local delivery is $4.00 within 3 km, the same delivery Grace runs for prescriptions. All prices are in Canadian dollars. The online shop can take an order for these goods only. It cannot dispense a prescription.

On the shelf

What is on the shelf

The Weekly Pill Organiser is $14.00, in Medicine helpers. It is a seven-day box with morning and evening, and no lettering on the case. The Digital Thermometer is $19.00, in Home care. The Travel First-Aid Pouch is $28.00, in Travel: a warm grey canvas pouch with plain plasters and gauze.

Unscented Hand Balm, 75 ml, is $16.00, in Skin, a plain tube and a small tin. The Linen Heat Pack is $18.00, in Home care. The Cotton Wrist Support is $24.00, in Home care. The first four sit by the till. The heat pack and the wrist support are on the same shelf.

Questions

Questions about a product

Questions about a product? Ask the pharmacist at the counter or call (416) 555-0148. We will tell you if something should stay on the shelf. A blister pack of prescribed medicine is not one of these products. That service is $6.00 per week and is prepared by Samuel in the dispensary.

The pill organiser is only an empty box you fill yourself from medicines already talked through. Email counter@megumipharmacy.example if you want an item held. Hours are Monday to Friday 8:30–19:00, Saturday 9:00–17:00, Sunday 10:00–14:00. Statutory holidays are closed.

Plan your visit

posts.title: One list instead of twelve boxes
posts.excerpt: Ruth, 78, brought a shopping bag of medicines to a review with Leila Haddad and left with one written list.
posts.content:
Ruth arrived on a weekday morning with a canvas shopping bag. She is 78. Inside were twelve boxes and a few loose bottles, some from this pharmacy and some she had kept at home. She set the bag on the consultation table and said she was no longer sure which box belonged to which meal.

Leila Haddad met her in the consultation room. A medicine review here is 30 minutes, by appointment, and the fee is $35.00. Leila asked Ruth to empty the bag onto the table. They did not start with a new prescription. They started with what was already in the house.

The two of them sorted the boxes into rows. Leila read each one against the record Megumi Pharmacy has kept for Ruth at 1184 Queen Street East. She asked about allergies and about any medicine from another prescriber. That check is the same habit we use when a prescription is handed in. It takes about ten minutes of looking before anything is prepared or changed.

Ruth had been taking a morning tablet from one box and an evening tablet from another, and she was not certain both were still current. Leila did not tell her to stop or start anything in the room. She wrote one list: the name of each medicine, the time of day, and whether it was still on the record. Where a box looked duplicated, she marked it and said she would speak with Ruth’s doctor before any change.

A change, when one is needed, is written down for the prescriber. It is not made quietly in the consultation room. Ruth left with her own copy. The pharmacy kept a copy with her record. Nothing was promised about how she would feel later. The review is a conversation about what is in front of you. We do not describe it as a settled result.

Two weeks later Leila called. That is what we do after a review that shifts a routine, and it is what we do after every new long-term medicine. She asked whether the single list was easier to follow than the shopping bag, and whether any box was still unclear. Ruth said she felt more confident laying the medicines out at breakfast. She did not say she was well, and we would not have written that if she had. Confidence with a list is as far as this story goes.

The same morning, Grace Liu was on the front counter and Samuel Brandt was in the dispensary, checking a label against a box. If Ruth’s doctor sends a change, it can arrive as paper, as an e-prescription, or as a repeat request by phone or by email to counter@megumipharmacy.example. A new prescription is usually ready in 20 minutes. A repeat is ready within 24 hours. We say usually, because a question about the record can take longer, and we would rather pause than rush a label past a doubt.

Weekly blister packs are there if a list on paper is still too much to follow at home. Samuel prepares them each week. The fee is $6.00 per week. Home delivery, if the walk to Queen Street East is hard, is $4.00 within 3 km. Pickup at the counter has no delivery charge. None of these extras was added to Ruth’s bag during the review. Leila does not turn a half hour about medicines into a tray of things to buy.

Megumi Ward opened this independent pharmacy in 2006 so a conversation like Ruth’s could happen at a named counter, with the same people week after week. In 2011 the consultation room was added, and Leila uses it for reviews. The door stays ajar when the room is free. Beyond it is the same bright floor you see from the street: low shelves, a pale stone counter, and no pressure to add anything beside the medicine you already came in with.

We will not promise a result. We will not tell you the review will make you feel a certain way. If you want the same half hour Ruth had, ask for a medicine review at the counter or call (416) 555-0148. Bring everything you take, including the boxes you are unsure about. The appointment is 30 minutes and the fee is $35.00. All prices are in Canadian dollars. You leave with your copy of the list, and a pharmacist you can ask for by name the next time you come in.

The information in this story is general and does not replace advice from your pharmacist or doctor. Ruth is a fictional first name, used so the morning can be told without pointing at a neighbour. The six people on the rota are the people who work here: Megumi, Daniel Osei, Leila, Ana Kovač, Samuel, and Grace. If your own list is the thing that is tangled, bring the bag. We will sort it into rows and talk it through.

posts.title: Repeat prescriptions by email
posts.excerpt: Send a repeat request by email and collect it within 24 hours.
posts.content:
You can now send a repeat prescription request by email to counter@megumipharmacy.example, as well as by phone on (416) 555-0148 or at the counter. Please include your full name and the medicines you need.

Repeat prescriptions are ready within 24 hours. A pharmacist still checks each one against your record, and we call you if anything needs a conversation first.

posts.title: Holiday opening hours
posts.excerpt: The pharmacy is closed on statutory holidays; the usual hours apply on the days around them.
posts.content:
Megumi Pharmacy is closed on statutory holidays. On every other day our hours are Mon–Fri 8:30–19:00, Sat 9:00–17:00 and Sun 10:00–14:00.

If you take a medicine every day, please send a repeat request by email or phone a few days before a holiday so that it is ready within 24 hours of the request.
